name: rolled oats pie top
instructions:
A food-processor rolled-oats topping for fruit pies — my alternative to a streusel-style crumble.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 3/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 3/4 cup rolled oats
- 1 cup brown sugar
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, COLD
- 1/4 tsp salt

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. All of it goes in a food processor — the unsalted butter goes in COLD. Process into a crumbly topping.
2. Scatter over a filled fruit pie and bake per the pie's recipe.
notes:
=== ORIGIN — BUILT FOR THE PEAR CRUMBLE ===

Developed as the topping for [[pear-crumble]], in place of Nicole Rucker's streusel-like ginger crumble (flour + sugars + melted butter). Used there successfully.

=== LESS FLOUR/BUTTER THAN A STREUSEL — MORE FREE LIQUID IN THE PIE ===

Compared to a streusel crumble, this runs less flour/butter, so the pie ends up with more overall liquid from the filling. In [[pear-crumble]] that surplus gets put to work: brush the outside of the pie crust with the filling's liquid drippings before baking, as a glaze.

=== COLD BUTTER, FOOD PROCESSOR ===

The butter goes in cold — the food processor cuts it through the flour/oats/sugar into a crumbly topping (pie-crust logic, not melted-butter streusel logic).

=== WHEN A PIE NEEDS A TOP ===

Hard fruits want coverage to cook through and come together. Pears are harder than apples when not ripe — [[pear-crumble]] NEEDS a topping like this (or a full pie lid), unlike [[apple-pie]] which is OK with a covered → uncovered bake.
